newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian shares reverse rally, Bombay index off 2 pct.
newsitem.headline: Indian shares reverse rally, Bombay index off 2 pct.

text.p: Shares across India retreated on Thursday as confidence in a day-old rally petered out with focus shifting to shaky fundamentals, brokers said.
The benchmark 30-stock Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) index fell 61.10 points, or 2.08 percent, to 2,880.26 after rallying 5.1 percent on Wednesday.
Traders said Wednesday's rally was propelled by misconceptions of an economic revival and government incentives in the first quarter of 1997.
"(Such) hopes will be belied as fundamentals continue to deteriorate," broking firm ING Barings said.
"We continue to believe that the bear phase has not yet run its full course," the firm said. "It is a good opportunity to restructure portfolios."
Analysts said doubts remained on the government's ability to offer sops to revive sagging markets and industrial output.
"The near-term scenario is pretty grim," said Sunil Kothari at broker Nagindas Kothari. "There's distinct possibility of petrol (and other fuels) prices being raised very soon."
The 50-share National Stock Exchange index fell 9.82 points to 827.25 with the net traded value at 9.92 billion rupees in 49.16 million shares.
The 500-share CRISIL index eased 6.03 points to 557.09. But CRISIL's mid-cap 200-stock index gained 5.27 points to 384.28.
The Delhi index lost 14.07 points to 647.95, Calcutta index 5.68 to 397.08 and Madras index 38.09 to 2,933.05.

Cement production and despatches in November were higher than in October, latest industry figures showed but shares of cement firms were hit by sellers. ACC fell 39.50 rupees to 1,000 and Gujarat Ambuja Cement shed 6.50 to 221.50.
TELCO dropped 10 rupees to 318, M&M 4.0 to 311 and Bajaj Auto 0.50 to 723. SBI lost 7.50 rupees to 209, Reliance 7.25 to 187.50 and TISCO 6.75 to 153.75.
